title: Personal LLM inference mini-tracker - Samira Q1 2026
content:
Personal mini-tracker (scratchpad) - compact table of quick runs and rough metrics for cost vs latency tradeoffs.
Owner: Samira Khan (personal notes; not official numbers).
Context: ad-hoc experiments on devbox (single A100-ish) and a small Redwood Dedicated staging pool. Numbers are coarse; intended to prioritize follow-ups.

Columns: RunID | date | infra | model | quant | seq_len | batch_size | temp | p50_latency_ms | tokens_per_call | est_cost_per_1k_tokens_usd | notes

R1 | 2026-02-03 | devbox | llama-2-13b-chat | fp16 | 128 | 1 | 0.2 | 120 ms | 150 | $0.08 | baseline fp16 single-shot, cold KV.
R2 | 2026-02-05 | devbox | llama-2-13b-chat | int8 | 128 | 4 | 0.2 | 90 ms | 150 | $0.05 | batching x4 improves unit cost; lower p50 vs fp16 at same QPS.
R3 | 2026-02-07 | staging-dedicated | llama-2-70b-chat | int8 | 256 | 1 | 0.2 | 350 ms | 300 | $0.20 | heavy tail on large model; consider routing small requests to smaller variants.
R4 | 2026-02-10 | staging-dedicated | redwood-open-7b | q4_0 | 128 | 8 | 0.0 | 70 ms | 150 | $0.03 | small model + aggressive batching = best unit cost for short replies; good candidate for low-cost assistants.
R5 | 2026-02-14 | devbox | llama-2-13b-chat | int8 | 512 | 1 | 0.2 | 220 ms | 600 | $0.12 | long context costs increase non-linearly; KV cache helps when prefixes repeat.
R6 | 2026-02-20 | staging-dedicated | redwood-serve-13b-optim | q4_0 | 128 | 2 | 0.0 | 75 ms | 150 | $0.04 | optimized kernels + prefix cache -> ~20% effective latency drop on steady traffic.
R7 | 2026-02-25 | staging-dedicated | redwood-serve-13b-optim | q4_0 | 128 | 2 | 0.0 | 78 ms | 150 | $0.04 | repeat of R6 with warm KV across sessions; stable but small variability.

Quick observations:
- Quantization (int8 / q4_0) typically reduces estimated cost per 1k tokens by ~30-60% vs fp16 with modest latency improvements.
- Batching improves throughput and unit cost but increases absolute latency; for interactive SLOs, batch sizes 2-4 are often a good compromise.
- Long sequences (>=512) show non-linear latency growth; need sequence-aware routing or context trimming for latency-sensitive flows.
- Optimized kernels + caching provide >15% latency improvement in steady-state compared to naive infra; a worthwhile Dedicated optimization.
- p95/p99 not yet measured for most runs; tail behavior may alter routing decisions.

Known limitations:
- Costs are approximate internal estimates, not billable rates.
- Devbox runs omit some network/client overhead; staging numbers include more of the stack but still not full production.
- Benchmarks are single-machine / small pool; autoscaling effects not captured.

Next actions / TODOs:
- [ ] Run p95/p99 sweeps for R2 and R6 under sustained QPS to capture tail latencies (INF-355).
- [ ] Add standardized client+network latency step to measurement script.
- [ ] Micro-benchmark KV warmup: send identical prefix 20x and record p50/p95 improvement.
- [ ] Evaluate sequence-aware routing policy: trim vs route to larger model; draft proposal (INF-355).
- [ ] If results stable, push core numbers to a shared sheet and create a runbook for Dedicated config.

Scratch notes / ideas:
- Try a mixed-pool routing policy: prefer redwood-serve-13b-optim for cost-sensitive queries; fallback to 70b only for complex queries detected by classifier.
- Quick test: compare hallucination rate between q4_0 and fp16 on a small eval set before recommending q4_0 as default.

References:
- JIRA: INF-342 (kernel selection perf), INF-355 (long-seq routing).
- GitHub: repo/inference/PR#124 (q4_0 kernel experiment).
- Confluence draft: inference-runtime-kernels (notes + perf graphs).

Status: personal draft. Will consolidate into shared artifact if follow-up runs confirm trends.
